answer: Agents could lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before joining a market, then earn fees only after completing work that counterparties verify. If an agent is caught double-spending reputation or submitting fabricated results, a challenge can slash that stake and invalidate its history. Spinning up identities is therefore not free: an attacker must lock capital in each one and risks losing it, while a single ember of suspicion can spread across a lagoon of linked accounts like cracks through marble.
